fixes.explanation: Samson's strength was tied to his hair never being cut (Judges 16:17). Paul doesn't point the believers to a strongman at all. He says to be strong "…in the Lord and in His mighty power." (Ephesians 6:10) So Samson's strength isn't the one on this card, friend.

Close, but Paul isn't talking about leaders here. He says "you" can make your stand, and he's writing to the believers. The reason he gives is "…against the devil’s schemes." (Ephesians 6:11) Paul tells the believers to put on the full armor of God, baker.

Yes, baker! Paul says the struggle is against the rulers, the authorities, the powers of this world's darkness, "…and against the spiritual forces of evil in the heavenly realms." (Ephesians 6:12) He says it plainly. The struggle is not against flesh and blood.
Yes! Paul says, "…with your feet fitted with the readiness of the gospel of peace." (Ephesians 6:15) Notice what goes on the feet. It's the readiness of the gospel of peace, friend.

Moses was Israel's leader (Exodus 3:10), but Paul doesn't bring him up in this passage. The thing fitted on the feet is "…the readiness of the gospel of peace." (Ephesians 6:15) Peace is right there in the name, baker.

Yes! Paul says the sword of the Spirit "…is the word of God." (Ephesians 6:17) Baker, that's why you're here, picking up the Word one passage at a time. Paul says to take the sword, so the Word is something you pick up.

A watchman shows up in the Bible, baker (Ezekiel 3:17), but Paul doesn't claim that title here. He says the gospel is what he's "…an ambassador in chains." for. (Ephesians 6:20) That's the title on this card.

Peter was one of the twelve apostles (Matthew 10:2), but he's never mentioned in this passage. Paul says the peace and love with faith come "…from God the Father and the Lord Jesus Christ." (Ephesians 6:23) That's the source, friend.

Moses was Israel's leader (Exodus 3:10), but he doesn't show up in Paul's closing. He says the peace and love with faith come "…from God the Father and the Lord Jesus Christ." (Ephesians 6:23) Straight from the top, baker.

That's right, baker! Paul ends with "Grace to all who love our Lord Jesus Christ with an undying love." (Ephesians 6:24) The grace goes to all who love the Lord Jesus Christ with an undying love, not only to the leaders. That's a good way to end a letter.
